scope: Where the Rust rewrite's structure still differs from the Go owner it ports. Known source-confirmed gaps only, not an exhaustive acceptance claim.

findings.finding: A query, INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE is checked over the visit infos of the build that plans it (`table_privilege::check_plan_privilege`: a query's before it is optimized, a DML's once it is built, a point plan's through `check_fast_plan_privilege`). PREPARE and a new non-prepared plan-cache entry still collect their `VisitInfos` with the visit-only builds `query_visit_info` / `dml_visit_info` (`Session::collect_table_privileges`) and build their plans separately, where Go's `GeneratePlanCacheStmtWithAST` keeps those of its one `PlanBuilder.Build`; and an INSERT's visit infos come from the separate builders of its target, source and values, where Go's `buildInsert` has one `PlanBuilder`

findings.group: DDL: migrate responsibility before deleting implementations
findings.finding: 53 of Go's 86 `ddl.executor` methods (`pkg/ddl/executor.go`) have no counterpart, `DoDDLJob` / `DoDDLJobWrapper` among them: a statement is lowered into this port's own `DdlStatement` (`cluster_ddl.rs` `lower_ddl_with_context`, then a `lower_*` builder) and submitted by `submit_built_job` / `submit_persisted_job_with_retry`; the missing methods include `AlterSchema`, `CreateTableWithInfo` / `BatchCreateTableWithInfo`, `RebaseAutoID`, `ShardRowID`, `ChangeColumn`, `RenameColumn`, `RenameIndex`, `DropView`, `CreatePrimaryKey`, `LockTables`, `CleanupTableLock`, `RepairTable`, `CreateSequence` / `AlterSequence`, the placement-policy, check-constraint, masking-policy, TTL, cache and attribute alters

findings.group: DDL: migrate responsibility before deleting implementations
findings.finding: No ingest (fast-reorg) backfill: it falls back to the transactional merge (`tidb-ddl/src/cluster_ddl/add_index.rs`); with it the status port's `/ingest/*` routes (Go `IngestConcurrencyHandler` over `ingestctrl`'s rate-limit parameters) are absent

findings.group: DDL: migrate responsibility before deleting implementations
findings.finding: Cancellation follows Go's `convertJob2RollbackJob` for every action the worker runs. A columnar (vector, inverted, full-text) index is checked against its table as Go's `createColumnarIndex` does (`add_index.rs` `create_columnar_index`, `checkTableTypeForColumnarIndex`), but on a table with a columnar replica this node builds no `ActionAddColumnarIndex` job: `onCreateColumnarIndex` (TiFlash schema sync, `checkColumnarIndexProcess`) and its `rollingbackAddColumanrIndex` are absent

findings.group: DDL: migrate responsibility before deleting implementations
findings.finding: A multi-schema change has no `promoteProxyKVDiskFullPause`, whose only producer (`autoPauseAddIndexJobOnKVDiskFull`, the DXF add-index task) Rust lacks (D02, O10)

findings.group: DDL: migrate responsibility before deleting implementations
findings.finding: A persisted DDL job step takes its schema from the owner's `InfoCache` at the step's version (Go `jobCtx.infoCache`) with the job's involved schemas reloaded whole from meta (`overlay_job_schemas`: each `DBInfo` and every table in whatever state), and its action handlers look objects up in that catalog, where Go's handlers point-read the job's objects through `jobCtx.metaMut` (`checkSchemaExistAndCancelNotExistJob`, `GetTableInfoAndCancelFaultJob`)

Root HashAgg is Go's `HashAggExec` (`tidb-executor-aggregate/src/agg_hash_executor.rs`: fetcher, partial workers shuffling one mapper per final worker, final workers, `parallelHashAggSpillHelper` spill), and its serial and parallel memory are Go's to the byte for global and pushed-down aggregates (`sum(a)` 12.6 KB, `b, count(a) ... group by b` 13.5 KB, `count(distinct b)` 12.4 KB) (a grouped scan-fed `a, group_concat(b) ... group by a` 14.0 KB and an index-fed `count(distinct a)` 12.3 KB, as a Go statement loop that installs the connection's allocator charges them); its fetcher's capacity-0 input chunks fill through the select result's Go `Decoder` (`Decode` appends each buffer once and rounds its rows up to eight; `ReuseIntermChk` swaps a large remainder in), so a four-row VARCHAR-keyed response grows its input chunk by Go's 96 bytes (offsets 5/6) and `b, count(a) ... group by b`'s HashAgg peaks at Go's 13801 bytes; after earlier statements on one connection the workers' chunks receive the same recycled columns Go's do, but the charge still differs by what Go's `groupKeyPool` / `partialResultsBufferPool` keep across statements (the group_concat run after a `count(distinct a)`: Go 18.0 KB, this port 18.1 KB); a cop-side aggregation with no pushed form (`pushed_partial_aggregation` refuses its function kind, or an argument the pushdown catalog cannot lower: X01) runs in this tier on Go's TiDB-tier `HashAggExec` / `StreamAggExec`, where Go always runs it in the coprocessor; in the suites and the corpus only a TiFlash fragment's aggregates (M01) reach it

`IndexLookUpExecutor`'s memory and RU v2 are Go's, on every run: the double read (`IndexRangeSourceExec`, `access_path.rs` `IndexLookUpMemory`) owns a tracker labelled with its plan that each open attaches to the statement's, charged with its index ranges' KV ranges (`buildTableKeyRanges`), the index worker's responses (`LabelForIndexWorker`) and each table task's `executeTask` bytes (`cap(handles)` and the handles, the task's `TableReaderExecutor` at 768 plus its KV ranges and `dagPB.Size()`, the chunks it fills, `task.rows`, a keep-order `indexOrder` and `rowIdx`), the next task releasing the last; each task's reader records `TableReaderExecutor` into the parent's accumulator. EXPLAIN ANALYZE and `tidb_mem_quota_query` match Go for integer, keep-order `_tidb_rowid` and clustered handles (`tests_explain.rs` `an_index_lookup_charges_its_tasks_like_go`). The index worker's fetch chunk (`prepareHandleFetch`, typed by `getRetTpsForIndexReader`), each task reader's chunks (`TryNewCacheChunk`) and a serial projection's child chunk come from the session's allocator, so a task's charge follows the columns earlier statements returned to it, as Go's does (`an_index_lookup_takes_its_chunks_from_the_session_allocator_like_go`: `SELECT b, c FROM t USE INDEX(b) WHERE b > 1` charges 6.83 KB on a connection's first run and 14.1 KB after). A query's EXPLAIN ANALYZE result is written through a chunk taken from the allocator after the analyzed tree opens and before it runs (Go `ExplainExec`), and a pushed partial aggregate's tasks and a root `LimitExec` draw from it too, so a connection's statements reuse each other's columns as Go's do (`pipeline_mysql_client_source.rs` `a_connections_statements_reuse_each_others_chunks_like_go`). Under a pushed index-side Limit the index stream closes once the Limit is exhausted, before the task's reader charges it, as Go's index worker closes its result (`... LIMIT 64` 4.70 KB, `LIMIT 20` 2.47 KB: `an_index_lookup_under_a_pushed_limit_releases_its_index_response_like_go`). Remaining: the fetch chunk leaves out a keep-order merge's `byItems`; a task is exactly one `extractTaskHandles` batch (a whole 32-row response chunk through `ReuseIntermChk`), a table plan's Limit rides each task's request, a local index's partitioned task reads its rows without handles, and the table workers count every task they execute (`an_index_lookup_takes_one_response_chunk_per_task_like_go`); still, a table task takes its first chunk from the allocator after its response arrives, where Go's takes it before blocking on the request, so concurrent tasks take recycled columns in another order (`SELECT b, c FROM p USE INDEX(b) WHERE b > 90` over two partitions after a plain run: Go 4.45 KB, this port 12.3 KB); a partitioned lookup's index side is this port's native walk, so it has no response chunks to cut tasks at (`tidb_index_lookup_size = 2`: Go 4 tasks of up to 32 handles, this port 50 of 2); a task over a table-side partial aggregate is pushed for an unpartitioned integer-handle table only (a partitioned, common-handle or dirty read aggregates this tier's own lookups and charges nothing), and its group-by and AVG requests are 10 bytes smaller than Go's (`... GROUP BY c`: 5.71 KB where Go's shows 5.72 KB); a task (one `next_lookup_batch` window) is cut at the batch size where Go's `extractTaskHandles` keeps the whole chunk `readFromChunk` hands it (`ReuseIntermChk`), so a small batch splits Go's one task (6 rows at `tidb_index_lookup_size` 2: Go one 2.58 KB task, this port three, 4.92 KB), and a window spans the partitions Go gives a task each (`p ... PARTITION BY HASH(a) PARTITIONS 2`, `b > 1`: Go two tasks, 5.13 KB, this port one, 4.29 KB); a task the store answers without a table reader (`LookupFetch::LocalFallback`: a dirty transaction's read, a refused remote shape) charges nothing; a `LocalIndexLookUp`'s index-side responses hold handles where Go's hold the completed rows; and the reader is one source shared with `IndexReader` and index-merge partials, its tasks windows of one `LookupPipeline` over a `LanePool`, not Go's index worker, table workers and `resultCh`

`IndexJoin` and `IndexHashJoin` are Go's `IndexLookUpJoin` and `IndexNestedLoopHashJoin` (`join/index_lookup_join.rs`, `join/index_lookup_hash_join.rs`: outer and inner workers over `Joiner`), with Go's task memory and matching; the fused `JoinExec` lookup strategy is gone. Two gaps remain: Go's `IndexLookUpMergeJoin` executor (and `PhysicalIndexMergeJoin`'s `KeyOff2KeyOffOrderByIdx`, `CompareFuncs`, `NeedOuterSort`, `Desc`) is unported -- neither planner builds one on this branch, and the builder refuses the kind; and Go's `IndexJoinExecutorBuilder` builds each task's inner executor afresh, where this port's inner workers re-seed one shared `IndexLookupSource` under a lock unless the lookup forks (a common-handle prefix)

The embedded store's coprocessor runs every DAG through Go's `mppExec` chain (`tidb-unistore-cophandler` `mpp.rs`, `mpp_exec.rs`), filters condition by condition as Go's `VectorizedFilter` does, and answers errors as `genRespWithMPPExec` does (`SelectResponse.error`, a conflict's `OtherError`, an unsupported executor's `OtherError`), but the index-lookup push-down is absent end to end: a `LocalIndexLookUp` plan (the `index_lookup_pushdown` hint, `tidb_index_lookup_pushdown_policy`) runs as this tier's own double read (`physical_builder.rs` `lower_index_lookup_selections`) where Go's `IndexLookUpExecutor` sends one `IndexLookUp` DAG and reads its rows and `IntermediateOutputs`, and this tier's coprocessor refuses `buildIndexLookUp`

A TiKV reader builds its DAG from its access path's scan request (`cop_reader.rs`; `cop_plan_ids_for` matches executors to the pushed nodes by kind) where Go's `constructDAGReq` lowers the reader's pushed plan one node per executor (`ToPB`). A pushed TopN (a reader's, or an IndexLookUp's index side) reaches the coprocessor through the scan's offer, its `ByItem`s expressions over the scan's output as `PhysicalTopN.ToPB` lowers them. A covering `IndexReader`'s pushed Projection of columns is lowered as the request's Projection executor (over the scan, or over its pushed Selection through `accept_post_filter_projection`), and a covering reader over a pushed Selection returns only its `OutputColumns`, as Go's `dagReq.OutputOffsets`, under a pushed Limit too (the in-reader Limit narrows its source once the Selection is in: `SELECT a FROM t WHERE c > 2 LIMIT 3`'s reader charges Go's 295 Bytes); a covering reader decodes its response straight into its parent's chunk (Go `e.result.Next(ctx, req)`) when the request returns exactly its columns; but a pushed Projection that computes expressions is not lowered into the request (it runs as a local executor over the scan's whole row)

A projection's vectorized result column takes the shape its Go builtin's `vecEval*` gives it (`chunk_executor.rs`: `Resize*`, `Reserve*` and appends, one argument evaluated into it, a column's `CopyReconstruct`) for arithmetic, comparisons and `IN`, logic, `NOT`/`IS NULL`/`IS TRUE`, casts, `IF`/`IFNULL`/`CASE`/`COALESCE`, `GREATEST`/`LEAST` (a string one ping-pongs `result` with two buffers, reserving it before its rows land), the math, time, JSON, info and common string builtins, `ADDTIME`/`SUBTIME`, `CONVERT_TZ`, `ANY_VALUE` and `SETVAR`; a tree holding a builtin outside that table still appends row by row: the less common string, encryption and miscellaneous builtins; a string `GREATEST`/`LEAST` shapes `result` as Go's kernels do (`Evaluator::run`'s `string_extremum_vec`: the direct signature's ping-pong appends a computed first argument's rows, then each even step's running value after a `ReserveString(n)`, and copies an even count's last step in by `CopyConstruct`; the compare-as-time signature evaluates every argument into `result` before its values), and a compare-as-time call is built as Go's is (its signature kept from the uncast arguments, every argument cast to a string, `doTimeConversionForGL`'s truncation and `checkMonthDay` warnings, a `strconv.Atoi` failure raised as 1105). Elsewhere a variable-width argument a builtin evaluates into its `result` (`VecResult::Arg`) is shaped without the rows Go appends. The values still come from the row and batch evaluators rather than Go's `vecEval*` kernels, but under Go's `EvalExpr` choice (`vecEnabled && expr.Vectorized()`, scoped per projected expression and per filter; a Selection reads `tidb_enable_vectorized_expression` as Go's `SelectionExec` does) a string `GREATEST`/`LEAST` answers the later of two equal arguments as `vecEvalString` does, where a folded constant or a row evaluation keeps the earlier (`evalString`); a tree this port's `vectorized` table does not cover still answers the row value, and `IF`'s row fallback when its condition warns (`fallbackEval*`, which resizes) is not modelled

The session's reusable chunk allocator is Go's (`Session::chunk_alloc`, Go `clientConn.chunkAlloc`: installed per statement as `NewSyncAllocator(alloc)` under `tidb_enable_reuse_chunk`, never for an internal `InRestrictedSQL` statement, reset between statements and recreated after a failed one, each statement's validity its own), executors take it as `ExecutorMeta::alloc_pool` (Go `AllocPool`) for `NewChunk` / `TryNewCacheChunk` / `NewChunkWithCapacity`, and Go's `NewFirstChunk` sites (`Executor::new_first_chunk`: projection workers, hash-join probe and result chunks, index-hash-join results, shuffle holders, the drained record set) allocate outside it, so memory charges match Go's in sequence (`a_projection_sizes_its_result_columns_as_go_vec_eval_does`, `explain_analyze_dml_roots_report_their_executor_stats_and_memory_like_go`). The connection writes a result through a chunk from the statement's allocator (`writeChunks`' `rs.NewChunk(GetChunkAllocator())`, `ResultSetSource::new_write_chunk`), and a covering `IndexReader` returns its `OutputColumns` from the source itself (`dagReq.OutputOffsets`) instead of through a projection's pooled chunk, so a later statement reuses the same columns Go's does: a point UPDATE's root charges Go's 638 / 889 Bytes / 1.11 KB over the wire after a point UPDATE, `select 1` or a scan (`pipeline_mysql_client_source.rs` `explain_for_connection_charges_reused_chunks_like_go`). Remaining: executors built outside the physical builder's `meta` (`ExecutorMeta::new` in other crates and builder arms) allocate fresh; a materialized result (a plain EXPLAIN, SHOW and the other row-built statements) takes its write chunk from the allocator when its rows are already built (`a_plain_explain_and_a_show_write_through_pooled_chunks_like_go`, against the server binary), so a statement whose Go executor draws from the allocator before `Next` builds its rows (an EXPLAIN ANALYZE of a write, whose `ExplainExec` runs the write in `Next`) takes it after those draws; parallel apply's chunks, whose executor shape differs from Go's, are unmapped; the reuse hook's `StmtCtx.SetUseChunkAlloc` (`@@last_sql_use_alloc`) is not driven by allocation.
IMPORT INTO refuses (`tidb-session/src/dispatch.rs`)

A text `EXECUTE` of a cached prepared write runs inside the `EXECUTE`'s one statement lifecycle (`execute_cached_prepared_dml` no longer opens a nested `run_with_columns_using`), so it has one `StatementMemory` tracker, as Go's one `StmtCtx` does. The process plan follows Go's `SetProcessInfo`. A binary-protocol EXECUTE publishes no plan of its own (`runStmt`'s nil `currentPlan`), so the process info keeps the last valid plan, its brief binary plan and its collector. A SET, USE, DDL or transaction-control statement's plan renders no rows under `EXPLAIN FOR CONNECTION`. Both match a Go tidb-server over the wire (`unistore_cop.rs` `explain_for_connection_follows_gos_process_plan`). Remaining: a binary-protocol `EXECUTE` (`cluster_session_node` `execute`) binds its cached point, SELECT or DML plan before the statement lifecycle begins, so a plan-cache miss builds its planner context under the previous statement's authority, which `begin_statement_execution` then retires. Go's `ExecuteStmt` runs `PrepareTxnCtx` and `ResetContextOfStmt` before `Compile`'s plan-cache lookup.

`ReportMinStartTS` has no InfoCache recent-schema TS (`GetAndResetRecentInfoSchemaTS`, InfoSchema V2: I04). Lazy cursor fetch answers Go's `executor.Detach` over the physical plan (`tidb_executor::detach`), because the builder's operator tree is not Go's executor tree

No cross-keyspace runtime (null keyspace only); the next-gen-only surfaces built on it have no port either: the status port's `/dxf/*` and `/ddl/check/*`, and plan replayer's `tidb_cloud_storage_uri` storage (`pkg/planner/extstore` `createGlobalExtStorage`, local files on a classic kernel)

The MPP coordinator lowers a hand-built single-fragment scan DAG and refuses every pushed Selection, TopN and aggregation, where Go builds the fragment/task graph from the physical plan (including disaggregated compute placement)

`pkg/executor/mppcoordmanager` (`MPPCoordinatorManager`: coordinator registration, `detectAndDelete` expiry, the server address) and the RPC server's `ReportMPPTaskStatus` have no port, so TiFlash's task-status reports reach no coordinator; Go's coordinator only asks TiFlash for reports when its plan has a Limit above the table reader (`needReportExecutionSummary`), which the single-fragment scan never builds (M01)

PD's `serviceDiscovery` (`servicediscovery/service_discovery.go`) is not one owner here: member updates and the leader connection live in `pd/cluster.rs` / `pd/retry.rs`, with no per-member `serviceClient`, no `apiCandidateNodes` / `GetServiceClientByKind` (how Go picks a follower for a follower-handled region API) and no `checkServiceModeChanged`
No Cascades memo exploration/implementation in the production optimizer

A write's statement context is a second builder chain (`stmt_ctx_build.rs` `session_statement_context`'s DML branch) beside the query's; it carries the rule blacklist and `tidb_distsql_scan_concurrency`, but not `tidb_store_batch_size`, the rate-limit OOM action, `tiflash_replica_read` or `tidb_opt_derive_topn`, which Go's `SetFromSessionVars` and optimizer read for every statement (no observable effect found for these four: a Go server derives no TopN in a write's read either, and the single embedded store never batches a write's region tasks)

SQL/PB signature construction and typed vector execution. The planner's `BuiltinFunctionUsageInc` (`expressionRewriter.newFunction`) is not called: it needs the function's `PbCode`, which a planner-built Rust function only gets at pushdown resolution. Go's `PbConverter` sends each builtin's own `PbCode`; this port resolves a signature again from the function's name, argument types and planned result type (`pushdown_catalog.rs` `resolve`), a second copy of each function class's signature choice that covers the functions Go's `scalarExprSupportedByTiKV` pushes. The planner decides pushability from `infer_pushdown.rs`'s name list and the executor again from that catalog's resolvability: two authorities where Go reads the builtin's `PbCode` once.
No lazy InfoSchema V2, schema-cache-size loader/evictor or InfoCache timestamp ranges
BRIE statements are classified but never executed
No DXF scheduler/executor managers composed

TopSQL is ported over pprof-rs (`tidb-cpuprofile`, `tidb-topsql-collector`, `tidb-topsql-reporter`, `tidb-topsql`): the status port serves `TopSQLPubSub`, the single-target sink reports to `top-sql.receiver-address`, each command labels its thread `{connID}_{sqlID}`, each statement registers its SQL and plan and labels the thread with both digests, and the profiler's TiDB CPU reaches PROCESSLIST and the statement summary. The DDL worker attaches each job step and each backfill task to the job's SQL (`tidb-ddl` `job_ctx.rs`, Go `ReorgContext.attachTopProfilingInfo`). The step's transaction carries the job's resource-group tagger (`getResourceGroupTaggerForTopSQL`, published into its statement kv context once the step loads the job). Unported: the DXF backfill executor's attach (O10) and the fast-reorg skip checks' (`checkIfTableReorgWorkCanSkip` / `checkIfTempIndexReorgWorkCanSkip`, D02), and the multi-statement prefetch's plan hand-off: `prefetchPointPlanKeys` reads (or locks) the point writes' keys before the statements run (`cluster_session_node/prefetch.rs`, with its `setResourceGroupTaggerForMultiStmtPrefetch`), but its point plans are not handed to the statements (Go `PointPlanKey`), which plan again. Executors register the statement's SQL and plan on their first `Next` with Top profiling on (`RegisterSQLAndPlanInExecForTopProfiling`, `SqlKillerCheckExec`); profiler labels follow Go's goroutine inheritance (`labels::inherit`) into the shuffle, hash-join build, checksum, coprocessor, slow-log parse, cluster-table fan-out, analyze and global-stats merge, DDL analyze workers and the MPP client's store probes

The DDL scheduler, systable manager, history and MDL readers scan records instead of running SQL on `DdlSessionPool::sess_pool`; the bootstrap stages raw rows; accounts load eagerly where Go loads per active user

Go's `ExecRestrictedSQL` / `ExecuteInternal` are methods of the issuing session (`withRestrictedSQLExecutor`); this port's executors are adapters beside it (`NodeRestrictedSql`, `SystemSqlExecutor`, `ClusterStatsSqlExecutor`, the plan replayer's `SessionSql`). The node's two apply `ExecOption`'s `SnapshotTS`, `AnalyzeVer`, `AnalyzeSnapshot`, `EnableDDLAnalyze` and `PartitionPruneMode` and restore them as Go's `useCurrentSession` / `getInternalSession` do, but with no issuing session they cannot inherit `OptimizerUseInvisibleIndexes` / `SkipMissingPartitionStats` or append the internal session's warnings to the caller's (`IgnoreWarning`), and `ClusterStatsSqlExecutor` honours the options on the auto-analyze path alone. `rebuildSysVarCache` consumes the rows the domain's sysvar reload loop last read (`SysVarCacheDeps::table_contents`) where Go's runs `fetchTableValues` itself

The executable defaults `host` to `127.0.0.1` (`NodeConfig::deployment_defaults`) where Go's default is `0.0.0.0`, so a node started without `--host` advertises the loopback address (`INSTANCE` columns, server info) where Go's advertises `util.GetLocalIP()`; the loopback default goes with this port's refusal of a non-loopback listener under `--auth-file`, which Go has no counterpart of
